subject: dsa
title: Pow(x, n)
summary: Instead of multiplying x by itself n times, square repeatedly to build x^1, x^2, x^4, x^8, ... Then read n in binary and multiply together the squared powers whose bits are set.
problem: Compute x raised to the power n efficiently, in O(log n) multiplications rather than O(n).

steps.caption: Computing 2^10 the slow way is ten multiplications. Square repeatedly instead: 2^1, 2^2, 2^4, 2^8 — each cell is the one before it, squared.
Each power is the square of the previous: 2 -> 4 -> 16 -> 256. Just four steps reach 2^8.
Write the exponent in binary: 10 = 1010 = 8 + 2. So 2^10 = 2^8 * 2^2.
Pick the squared powers for the set bits: 2^2 = 4 and 2^8 = 256.
Multiply them: 256 * 4 = 1024 = 2^10, found in just a handful of multiplications.
